target.body:
## Summary

Adds tooltips and accessible labels for the Sessions table **Thinking** and
**Reasoning** controls (issue #90445), clarifying that:

- **Thinking** maps to the provider `reasoning_effort` and only applies when the
  model supports it (`compat.supportsReasoningEffort`).
- **Reasoning** controls how reasoning output is shown in chat (display/transport).

The column headers get `title` tooltips, and each per-row `<select>` gets a
`title` + `aria-label` so the meaning is reachable by pointer and screen reader.

## Review follow-up

Addresses the ClawSweeper finding (regenerate Control UI locale outputs): the new
English strings (`sessionsView.thinkingTooltip`, `sessionsView.reasoningTooltip`)
are now propagated through `pnpm ui:i18n:sync`, so the generated locale bundles and
`.i18n` metadata stay in sync and the UI i18n drift gate (`pnpm ui:i18n:check`)
passes. Rebased onto current `main`.

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/ui/views/sessions.test.ts` → 27 passed.
- `node --import tsx scripts/control-ui-i18n.ts check` → all locales clean.
- `oxfmt --check` / `oxlint` clean on changed source.

Part of #90445 (Sessions table only; Quick Settings, inherit semantics, and docs remain open in the issue)

target.title: fix(gateway): bound busy channel health by real run age
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`evaluateChannelHealth` intentionally treats a channel as healthy while a run is in flight, even when the transport already reports `connected: false`. That busy override is meant to be bounded by a 25 minute stale ceiling, but the ceiling is measured from `lastRunActivityAt`, which the run-state heartbeat refreshes every 60 seconds for as long as any run is active.

If a per-message task hangs forever, for example a channel send blocking on a half-open or dead socket with no send timeout after the transport disconnected, `onRunEnd` never fires, the heartbeat keeps ticking, and `lastRunActivityAt` never ages past roughly 60 seconds. The `>= 25min` stuck branch, the only escape from busy-overrides-disconnected, becomes permanently unreachable. The account is then reported healthy forever by the channel health monitor (`if (health.healthy) continue`), the readiness probe (`src/gateway/server/readiness.ts`), and the `openclaw health` CLI (`src/commands/health.ts`). No restart fires and no operator-visible signal appears until the process is restarted. Transport disconnects mid-send with no send timeout are a normal production failure mode.

## Why This Change Was Made

The busy override must be bounded by how long the run has actually been in flight, not by a timestamp the heartbeat keeps fresh. A single hung run must eventually breach the stale ceiling.

Root cause, `src/gateway/channel-health-policy.ts` busy branch (before):

```ts
const runActivityAge =
  lastRunActivityAt == null
    ? Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY
    : Math.max(0, policy.now - lastRunActivityAt);
if (runActivityAge < BUSY_ACTIVITY_STALE_THRESHOLD_MS) {
  return { healthy: true, reason: "busy" };
}
return { healthy: false, reason: "stuck" };
```

`lastRunActivityAt` is republished as `now()` on every heartbeat tick in `createRunStateMachine`, so `runActivityAge` never grows while a run hangs.

Fix. `createRunStateMachine` now tracks each in-flight run's start time keyed by an opaque run handle returned from `onRunStart` and passed back to `onRunEnd`, and publishes the oldest still-active run's start as `activeRunStartedAt`. When the oldest run ends the reported start advances to the next-oldest, and it clears when no run is active. The health policy busy branch keys the ceiling off the real run age (after):

```ts
const runStartAge =
  activeRunStartedAt == null ? null : Math.max(0, policy.now - activeRunStartedAt);
const runActivityAge =
  lastRunActivityAt == null ? null : Math.max(0, policy.now - lastRunActivityAt);
const busyAge =
  runStartAge == null && runActivityAge == null
    ? Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY
    : Math.max(runStartAge ?? 0, runActivityAge ?? 0);
if (busyAge < BUSY_ACTIVITY_STALE_THRESHOLD_MS) {
  return { healthy: true, reason: "busy" };
}
return { healthy: false, reason: "stuck" };
```

Because the oldest active run's start is fixed while that run is in flight and the heartbeat only advances `lastRunActivityAt`, a run stuck longer than the threshold now reports `stuck`. Because the reported start is the oldest active run and advances as runs complete, a channel churning through many short overlapping runs stays healthy; only a genuinely hung run breaches the ceiling. The `activeRunStartedAt` field flows through the same run-state to snapshot path as `lastRunActivityAt` (`run-state-machine.ts` publish, `account-snapshot-fields.ts` read, `types.core.ts` snapshot type), so all three consumers of `evaluateChannelHealth` (monitor, readiness, CLI) get the corrected verdict.

## Why This Is The Right Boundary

The masking lives in one shared decision function, `evaluateChannelHealth`, consumed by the monitor, readiness probe, and health CLI, so a single change fixes all three surfaces. The heartbeat that defeats the ceiling lives in `createRunStateMachine`, the one owner of run activity status, so the run-age fact is surfaced where it is produced rather than re-derived per caller. `createChannelRunQueue` shares one run-state machine across all queue keys and `KeyedAsyncQueue` runs unrelated keys concurrently, so `activeRuns` routinely exceeds 1; tracking the oldest active run rather than a busy-streak start keeps a continuously busy account healthy while still catching a single hung run. Legitimate busy behavior is preserved: short, active, and overlapping runs stay healthy, and snapshots without a start time fall back to the previous `lastRunActivityAt` behavior. `onRunEnd` now takes the run handle returned by `onRunStart`; the only in-repo caller, `createChannelRunQueue`, is migrated in this same commit, and typed plugin consumers get a compile error rather than silent breakage. Restoring a no-argument `onRunEnd` overload was deliberately avoided because it would reintroduce the counter-decrement accounting this change removes and split run tracking across two paths. The 25 minute ceiling is the pre-existing `BUSY_ACTIVITY_STALE_THRESHOLD_MS` constant; this change only makes it reachable, so a single run in flight past it is now treated as stuck by design. This is distinct from PR #96198, which fixes the same class of heartbeat-hides-stuck bug in the agent diagnostic stuck-session detector (`src/agents/*`, `src/logging/diagnostic-run-activity.ts`), a different subsystem that does not touch channel health.

## User Impact

Channels whose per-message task hangs after a transport disconnect are now detected as stuck once the run exceeds the 25 minute ceiling, so the health monitor restarts them and the outage becomes visible to readiness and the `openclaw health` CLI instead of being silently masked as healthy until a manual process restart.

## Evidence

- New regression test in `src/gateway/channel-health-policy.test.ts`: a disconnected channel with a run in flight longer than the threshold and a fresh heartbeat now evaluates to `{ healthy: false, reason: "stuck" }`. Fails on pristine `main` (returns `busy`), passes with this patch. A companion case keeps a short-lived run `busy`.
- New tests in `src/channels/run-state-machine.test.ts`: across 26 minutes of heartbeat ticks `activeRunStartedAt` stays fixed at the run start while `lastRunActivityAt` advances; and when an older run ends while a newer run is still active the reported start advances to the next-oldest run, so overlapping short runs do not accumulate false age.
- Verification commands (from a deps-enabled checkout):
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/channel-health-policy.test.ts src/channels/run-state-machine.test.ts` passes on this patch.
  - Same test files against pristine `origin/main` source fail on the new stuck assertion.
  - `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs`, `oxfmt --check`, and `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs` (core and core-test) all clean on the changed files.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: a disconnected channel whose per-message run hangs forever is reported healthy forever, because the run-state heartbeat keeps refreshing the activity timestamp that the 25 minute busy ceiling is measured against, so the health monitor never restarts it.
Real environment tested: drove the real periodic health monitor loop from `startChannelHealthMonitor` (`src/gateway/channel-health-monitor.ts`) over the real `evaluateChannelHealth` (`src/gateway/channel-health-policy.ts`) fed by a live `createRunStateMachine` (`src/channels/run-state-machine.ts`) with its real `setInterval` heartbeat, on real wall-clock (`Date.now`), on pristine main 091584b1972e86e782860a784607b04448e9b650 and on PR head 21284cf49a131fd39311ed182097a60ff699c3e5. Only the channel transport was stubbed, at the narrowest seam (the `ChannelManager` the monitor calls), so the monitor's real restart recovery path stays observable. Executed on a remote Crabbox AWS lease (c7a.xlarge, eu-west-1, lease cbx_452e9479c6de), not on the author machine. The 25 minute busy ceiling and the 60 second heartbeat were both scaled down 300x (to 5 seconds and 200 milliseconds) so a genuinely hung run breaches the ceiling in seconds of real elapsed time rather than 26 minutes; nothing else was altered and both runs used identical scaling.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: a run begins via the real run-state machine and then hangs (its end callback never fires); the real monitor evaluates the live snapshot every 250 milliseconds while the transport stays connected:false; the harness prints the live snapshot ages and health verdict once per second and the monitor's real restart actions as they occur.
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine main 091584b, run hung well past the scaled ceiling)
[health-monitor] started (interval: 0s, startup-grace: 0s, channel-connect-grace: 3600s)
t=1.0s connected=false activeRuns=1 lastRunActivityAtAge=0.2s activeRunStartedAtAge=n/a -> healthy=true reason=busy
t=5.0s connected=false activeRuns=1 lastRunActivityAtAge=0.2s activeRunStartedAtAge=n/a -> healthy=true reason=busy
t=7.0s connected=false activeRuns=1 lastRunActivityAtAge=0.2s activeRunStartedAtAge=n/a -> healthy=true reason=busy
SUMMARY monitorRestarts=0 finalVerdict=busy
# AFTER (PR head 21284cf, identical inputs, identical 300x scaling)
[health-monitor] started (interval: 0s, startup-grace: 0s, channel-connect-grace: 3600s)
t=1.0s connected=false activeRuns=1 lastRunActivityAtAge=0.2s activeRunStartedAtAge=1.0s -> healthy=true reason=busy
t=4.0s connected=false activeRuns=1 lastRunActivityAtAge=0.2s activeRunStartedAtAge=4.0s -> healthy=true reason=busy
t=5.0s connected=false activeRuns=1 lastRunActivityAtAge=0.2s activeRunStartedAtAge=5.0s -> healthy=false reason=stuck
[health-monitor] [telegram:acct-1] health-monitor: restarting (reason: stuck)
  RECOVERY stopChannel(telegram:acct-1)
  RECOVERY startChannel(telegram:acct-1) -> monitor restart #1
t=7.0s connected=false activeRuns=1 lastRunActivityAtAge=0.2s activeRunStartedAtAge=7.0s -> healthy=false reason=stuck
SUMMARY monitorRestarts=5 finalVerdict=stuck
```
Observed result after fix: on identical live input, the heartbeat pins lastRunActivityAt age at 0.2s in both runs, so BEFORE the channel stays healthy and busy for the whole hang and the monitor never restarts it (monitorRestarts=0); AFTER, the fixed activeRunStartedAt age grows until it breaches the ceiling, the verdict flips to unhealthy and stuck, and the real health monitor completes its restart recovery path (stopChannel then startChannel) five times over the window. The one value that moves from wrong to right is the health verdict for a hung disconnected channel, and with it the monitor's restart action.
What was not tested: no live provider socket was hung end to end; the hang was a real never-resolving run under the real heartbeat, and the transport was a stub at the ChannelManager seam. The busy ceiling and heartbeat were scaled 300x on real wall-clock so the breach happens in seconds; the unscaled 25 minute breach was not waited out. Full build not run; the change is not on a lazy or packaging boundary.

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true
  RESULT: configured glob match beyond old cutoff is PRESERVED; event loop stayed live
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the cutoff removed, the configured `**/AGENTS.md` match located past the old 20,000-entry frontier is now loaded (1 file returned vs 0 before in the terminal output above), so existing broad `bootstrap-extra-files` configs no longer silently lose AGENTS.md/TOOLS.md context. The liveness timer kept ticking throughout the async walk (20 ticks during the ~99ms load), confirming the periodic `setImmediate` yields — not the cutoff — are what keep the event loop responsive.
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real glob-resolution code path and event-loop liveness directly rather than through a connected channel. The focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

Closes #87509

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
